Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: 33.01% exceeds the 20% threshold and 5.81 km exceeds the 0.8 km threshold. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The driver's answer is that PIE was closed and that LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02855-01 covers it. That artifact is MISSING from the bundle: its admissibility status is MISSING, its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. No advisory on file names any road or segment the optimal route traverses, carries no validity window, and cannot be matched to a route that leaves the optimal corridor before an affected segment and rejoins after. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable on the record and the driver's traffic assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08.

The driver's assertion cites the missing advisory identifier, so the comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run and the excuse falls away. The rider has shown an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold on a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) - 184 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 s. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route; the driver's traffic assertion neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

The refund is arithmetic. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 applies: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 23.8) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = 24.4640. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02855 and the pickup timestamp 2026-08-11T06:46:18+08:00.

claims.text: The rider's own trip record and the platform's GPS trace agree that this trip was driven 23.41 km against a booked optimal of 17.6 km. The governing figure under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 23.41 km, and the excess is 5.81 km, or 33.01% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 33.01% is greater than the 20% threshold and 5.81 km is greater than the 0.8 km threshold. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The driver's answer is that 'PIE was closed, LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02855-01 covers it.' That advisory is not in the bundle: EV-ADVIS-02855-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's external-traffic assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and where the bundle holds no advisory covering the trip window the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver's excuse therefore neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

The driver's assertion cites the missing advisory by its identifier, so this is not the POL-RD-13(1) case of an uncited excuse. But the trace itself is clean: 184 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No chat log exists for this trip: EV-CHAT-02855 carries 0 messages and no first or last message timestamp. There is therefore no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no rider-requested waypoint whose corroboration test could be run. The whole 5.81 km excess is unexplained on the record.

The trip record shows no amendment to either endpoint: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal exists to displace the booked 17.6 km baseline. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in play.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and POL-RD-11 does not. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 23.8) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 24.4640. The charged total is 30.69, so the refund is 30.69 - 24.4640 = 6.2260, rounded up to SGD 6.25. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.25.

The fare breakdown carries no ERP lines at all: erp_gantries is empty and the off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00. There is no off-route gantry charge to correct under POL-RD-09(2), and no phantom gantry line to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The refund is the distance-and-time figure alone, and no pass-through amount is added on top of it.

The excess of 5.81 km is greater than 50% of optimal? No - it is 33.01%, which is below the 50% materiality gate, and 5.81 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate. The deviation is established but NOT material, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows from it. I do not claim a repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 278, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test is met.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the trip identifier TRP-02855 matches across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, the pickup timestamp is consistent, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration condition for sub-30% claims is not engaged and no extra corroboration is required.

The driver's profile is clean on the only counters that may ground a finding: deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 278. I note for completeness that no_show_terminations_30d is 1, but that field belongs to POL-NS-07 and is not a route-deviation test; under POL-GEN-01 it is context only and I do not ask the judge to weigh it against the driver on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves while it is held. Both of you should understand the two findings that lead there.

1. The deviation is established. The governing distance is the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02855), which records 23.41 km, against the booked optimal of 17.6 km (EV-TRIP-02855). That is an excess of 5.81 km, or 33.01% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the rider's claim is made out on the trace figure; I have not used the rounded 23.4 km on the trip record, as POL-RD-01 requires the trace to govern. The trace is not impaired: EV-GPS-02855 carries 184 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage and no gaps, so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) is not engaged and POL-RD-10(3) does not fire. Nothing else excuses the excess either: there is no chat content (EV-CHAT-02855 has 0 messages), so POL-RD-04 cannot run; there was no endpoint amendment (pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null), so POL-RD-05 cannot run; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply; and the fare carries no ERP or surcharge line, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to correct.

2. On the arithmetic alone this would be a PARTIAL_REFUND. The fare is METERED (EV-FARE-02855), so POL-RD-02 gives recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 23.8) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP = SGD 24.4640; charged_total of SGD 30.69 less that is SGD 6.2260, rounded up to SGD 6.25. Both sides computed the same figure, and I accept it.

What stops that ruling is the driver's answer. The driver says PIE was closed and names LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02855-01. That advisory is not in the bundle: it is marked MISSING, its payload is null and its weight_multiplier is 0.0, with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. So POL-RD-03 cannot be run against it, and the traffic excuse carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Critically, because the driver named that identifier in his own answer, this is not the uncited-excuse case that POL-RD-13(1) keeps out of escalation: POL-RD-10(5) applies - an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact that is missing from the pool - and POL-RD-10(5) is terminal. I therefore rule ESCALATE rather than PARTIAL_REFUND, and the SGD 6.25 is neither paid nor collected; the disputed amount is held. The driver's argument, and the rider's agreement, that the case should simply proceed to the POL-RD-02 refund because POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged is correct about the trace but does not answer POL-RD-10(5), and is rejected.

On the profiles: POL-RD-06 is not triggered, because a 33.01% / 5.81 km excess is neither over 50% nor over 8.0 km and is therefore not a MATERIAL deviation; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 278, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral follows. No profile field that POL-GEN-01 makes context-only has been used as a ground of decision.

What would resolve this on review: a complete LTA traffic-advisory record covering the Tampines Mall corridor in the trip window (about 06:38-07:17 on 11 August 2026), which would let POL-RD-03 be tested properly; or confirmation that no such closure record exists, in which case the driver's excuse falls away on the merits and the POL-RD-02 arithmetic of SGD 6.25 is the figure the reviewer would consider.

Charged_total is 30.69, so the refund is 30.69 - 24.4640 = 6.2260, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 6.25. That is 20.29% of charged_total, well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a rider with 4 or more claims and 1 or fewer substantiated does not apply, and the trace alone carries the excess. The rider's burden under POL-RD-08(a) is met: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02855 and the pickup timestamp 2026-08-11T06:46:18+08:00.

No ERP or toll line needs separate treatment. The fare_breakdown carries 0.00 of ERP, no gantry lines and no airport surcharge, and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a charged gantry, so there is no pass-through correction to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4).

The driver's profile does not support a repeat-deviation uplift. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 278, so the ratio is 0.0, far below the 0.05 pattern threshold, and no POL-RD-06 pattern is established. The rider does not seek the FULL_REFUND uplift or a conduct referral on this record; the remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial refund of 6.25.

The rider's own trip record and the platform's GPS trace agree that this trip was driven 23.41 km against a booked optimal of 17.6 km. The governing figure under POL-RD-01 is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 23.41 km, and the excess is 5.81 km, or 33.01% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass: 33.01% is greater than the 20% threshold and 5.81 km is greater than the 0.8 km threshold. The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The driver's answer is that 'PIE was closed, LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-02855-01 covers it.' That advisory is not in the bundle: EV-ADVIS-02855-01 is MISSING, carries no payload and has weight_multiplier 0.0. Under POL-RD-13 the driver's external-traffic assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and where the bundle holds no advisory covering the trip window the comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver's excuse therefore neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

ledger.claim: The driver's assertion cites the missing advisory by its identifier, so this is not the POL-RD-13(1) case of an uncited excuse. But the trace itself is clean: 184 fixes at a 10 second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No chat log exists for this trip: EV-CHAT-02855 carries 0 messages and no first or last message timestamp. There is therefore no rider instruction that could exonerate any part of the excess under POL-RD-04, and no rider-requested waypoint whose corroboration test could be run. The whole 5.81 km excess is unexplained on the record.

The trip record shows no amendment to either endpoint: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null. POL-RD-05 cannot be run and no amended optimal exists to displace the booked 17.6 km baseline. The vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and the matched-itinerary baseline is not in play.

The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs the remedy and POL-RD-11 does not. The recomputed fare on the booked optimal route is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 + 0.28 x 23.8) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 24.4640. The charged total is 30.69, so the refund is 30.69 - 24.4640 = 6.2260, rounded up to SGD 6.25. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.25.

The fare breakdown carries no ERP lines at all: erp_gantries is empty and the off-optimal-route and on-optimal-route ERP totals are both 0.00. There is no off-route gantry charge to correct under POL-RD-09(2), and no phantom gantry line to refund under POL-RD-09(4). The refund is the distance-and-time figure alone, and no pass-through amount is added on top of it.

The excess of 5.81 km is greater than 50% of optimal? No - it is 33.01%, which is below the 50% materiality gate, and 5.81 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate. The deviation is established but NOT material, so the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows from it. I do not claim a repeat-deviation pattern: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 278, so neither limb of the POL-RD-06 test is met.

The rider's burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged: the trip identifier TRP-02855 matches across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, the pickup timestamp is consistent, and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The rider's profile shows deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration condition for sub-30% claims is not engaged and no extra corroboration is required.

The driver's profile is clean on the only counters that may ground a finding: deviation_flags_90d is 0 and completed_trips_90d is 278. I note for completeness that no_show_terminations_30d is 1, but that field belongs to POL-NS-07 and is not a route-deviation test; under POL-GEN-01 it is context only and I do not ask the judge to weigh it against the driver on this trip.
